sudan.title: حنين إلى «الرجل القوي».. قصة (8) ملايين مشاهدة لخبر وفاة نميري - سودان تربيون
sudan.summary: تجاوزت مشاهدات خبر وفاة الرئيس السوداني الأسبق جعفر نميري ثمانية ملايين مشاهدة، مما يعكس حنين الكثيرين إلى فترة حكمه. نميري، الذي تولى السلطة في عام 1969 حتى الإطاحة به في 1985، كان شخصية مثيرة للجدل في تاريخ السودان. بعض السودانيين يتذكرونه كـ "رجل قوي" ساهم في استقرار البلاد، بينما يعتبره آخرون رمزًا للقمع. الخبر أثار تفاعلات واسعة على وسائل التواصل الاجتماعي، حيث تبادل المستخدمون ذكريات وتجارب من فترة حكمه. يعكس هذا الاهتمام العميق بتاريخه تأثيره المستمر على الوعي الجمعي للسودانيين، رغم مرور عقود على سقوط نظامه.

sudan.title: أسفر هجوم بطائرة مسيرة في السودان عن مقتل 80 شخصاً. - Vietnam.vn
sudan.summary: أسفر هجوم بطائرة مسيرة في السودان عن مقتل 80 شخصاً، حيث استهدفت الغارة منطقة في ولاية دارفور. الهجوم يأتي في وقت يشهد فيه السودان تصاعداً في النزاع المسلح بين القوات الحكومية والمجموعات المسلحة. وقد أدان المجتمع الدولي هذا الهجوم، مطالباً بتحقيق شامل لتحديد المسؤولين عنه. كما أعربت منظمات حقوق الإنسان عن قلقها إزاء تصاعد العنف وتأثيره على المدنيين. الهجوم يعكس الوضع الأمني المتدهور في البلاد، حيث يعاني السكان من تداعيات النزاع المستمر.

sudan.title: مستجدات الشرق الأوسط: أكثر من 100 قتيل في هجمات بالمسيرات في أنحاء السودان - SBS
sudan.summary: أفادت التقارير أن أكثر من 100 شخص لقوا حتفهم في سلسلة من الهجمات التي نفذتها طائرات مسيرة في مختلف أنحاء السودان. تأتي هذه الهجمات في وقت يشهد فيه البلد تصاعدًا في النزاع المسلح، حيث تتزايد الاشتباكات بين القوات الحكومية والمجموعات المسلحة. وقد أدت هذه الأحداث إلى تفاقم الأوضاع الإنسانية في البلاد، مع تزايد أعداد النازحين والجرحى. كما دعت منظمات حقوق الإنسان إلى ضرورة اتخاذ إجراءات عاجلة لحماية المدنيين وتقديم المساعدات اللازمة للمتضررين من هذه الهجمات.

sudan.title: السودان: أكثر من 100 قتيل في هجمات بمسيّرات على كردفان ودارفور والخرطوم - France 24
sudan.summary: أفادت تقارير أن أكثر من 100 شخص لقوا حتفهم في هجمات شنتها طائرات مسيّرة في مناطق كردفان ودارفور والخرطوم بالسودان. الهجمات، التي تُعتبر من بين الأكثر دموية في الصراع المستمر في البلاد، استهدفت مدنيين وأدت إلى تدمير العديد من المنازل والبنية التحتية. وقد أثارت هذه الأحداث قلقاً دولياً متزايداً بشأن الوضع الإنساني في السودان، حيث يعاني السكان من نقص حاد في المساعدات الأساسية. الحكومة السودانية لم تصدر بعد بياناً رسمياً حول هذه الهجمات، لكن المنظمات الإنسانية تدعو إلى اتخاذ إجراءات عاجلة لحماية المدنيين وتقديم المساعدة للمحتاجين.

sudan.title: وزير الصحة يشارك في مؤتمر وجائزة ميدغلوبال بشيكاغو - سودان اندبندنت
sudan.summary: شارك وزير الصحة في مؤتمر وجائزة ميدغلوبال الذي أقيم في شيكاغو، حيث تم مناقشة قضايا الصحة العالمية والتحديات التي تواجهها الدول. المؤتمر جمع خبراء وصناع قرار من مختلف أنحاء العالم لتبادل الأفكار والخبرات في مجال الرعاية الصحية. كما تم تسليط الضوء على الابتكارات والحلول الممكنة لتحسين الخدمات الصحية. الوزير أعرب عن أهمية التعاون الدولي في مواجهة الأوبئة والأمراض المزمنة، وأكد على التزام السودان بتحسين النظام الصحي وتوفير الرعاية اللازمة للمواطنين.

sudan.title: مجلس الأمن والدفاع يوجه بالتصدي للمخططات المهددة للبلاد - سودان تربيون
sudan.summary: عقد مجلس الأمن والدفاع في السودان اجتماعًا لمناقشة التهديدات التي تواجه البلاد، حيث تم توجيه الجهات المعنية بالتصدي للمخططات التي تهدد الأمن القومي. وركز الاجتماع على التحديات الأمنية والسياسية التي يواجهها السودان، بما في ذلك الأزمات الداخلية والنزاعات. كما تم التأكيد على أهمية تعزيز التعاون بين القوات المسلحة والأجهزة الأمنية لضمان استقرار البلاد. وأشار المجلس إلى ضرورة اتخاذ إجراءات فورية لمواجهة هذه التهديدات وحماية المواطنين.

sudan.title: جوبا تستدعي السفير السوداني احتجاجًا على قصف سوق «النعام» في أبيي - سودان تربيون
sudan.summary: استدعت حكومة جوبا السفير السوداني احتجاجًا على القصف الذي استهدف سوق «النعام» في منطقة أبيي. وأعربت وزارة الخارجية في جنوب السودان عن إدانتها الشديدة لهذا الهجوم، الذي أسفر عن وقوع إصابات وأضرار مادية. وأكدت الحكومة أنها ستتخذ إجراءات دبلوماسية مناسبة للتعامل مع هذا الاعتداء، مشددة على أهمية الحفاظ على الأمن والاستقرار في المنطقة. يأتي هذا التصعيد في ظل التوترات المستمرة بين السودان وجنوب السودان، حيث تسعى جوبا إلى تعزيز العلاقات مع جيرانها وتفادي أي تصعيد عسكري.

sudan.title: السودان: أكثر من 100 قتيل في غارات بمسيّرات على كردفان ودارفور والخرطوم - Euronews.com
sudan.summary: أسفرت غارات جوية باستخدام مسيّرات عن مقتل أكثر من 100 شخص في مناطق كردفان ودارفور والخرطوم بالسودان. وتأتي هذه الهجمات في وقت يشهد فيه البلد تصاعدًا في النزاع المسلح بين القوات الحكومية والمجموعات المسلحة. وقد أدت الغارات إلى تدمير العديد من المنازل والبنية التحتية، مما زاد من معاناة المدنيين. كما تم الإبلاغ عن إصابة العشرات، مما يفاقم من الوضع الإنساني المتدهور في البلاد. وتستمر الدعوات الدولية لوقف الأعمال العدائية وتقديم المساعدات الإنسانية للمتضررين.

sudan.title: ذهب السودان المنهوب في الإمارات – الشروق أونلاين - الشروق أونلاين
sudan.summary: تتناول المقالة قضية الذهب المنهوب من السودان الذي يُهرّب إلى الإمارات. تشير التقارير إلى أن كميات كبيرة من الذهب تُستخرج بشكل غير قانوني في السودان، حيث تستفيد من ذلك شبكات تهريب منظمة. يُعتقد أن هذه الشبكات تعمل بالتعاون مع بعض الجهات في الإمارات، مما يسهل عملية التهريب ويعزز من تجارة الذهب غير المشروعة. يُظهر الوضع القائم كيف أن الفساد وضعف الرقابة في السودان يسهمان في تفشي هذه الظاهرة، مما يؤدي إلى فقدان البلاد لعائدات كبيرة من مواردها الطبيعية. كما تثير القضية تساؤلات حول دور الإمارات في هذه الأنشطة وكيفية تأثيرها على الاقتصاد السوداني.

sudan.title: لجنة المعلمين تعلن إضرابًا شاملًا في الخرطوم يومي الأربعاء والخميس - سودان تربيون
sudan.summary: أعلنت لجنة المعلمين في السودان عن إضراب شامل في العاصمة الخرطوم يومي الأربعاء والخميس القادمين. يأتي هذا الإضراب احتجاجًا على الأوضاع الحالية في قطاع التعليم، بما في ذلك نقص الموارد والظروف المعيشية الصعبة التي يواجهها المعلمون. وأكدت اللجنة أن الإضراب يهدف إلى الضغط على الحكومة لتحسين أوضاع المعلمين وتوفير بيئة تعليمية مناسبة للطلاب. كما دعت اللجنة جميع المعلمين إلى الالتزام بالإضراب والمشاركة في الفعاليات المقررة خلال هذه الأيام.

ethiopia.title: From Military Victory to Political Settlement - Why Ethiopia's Real Test Lies Beyond Controlling Mekelle
ethiopia.content: Ethiopia: From Military Victory to Political Settlement - Why Ethiopia's Real Test Lies Beyond Controlling Mekelle - allAfrica.com AllAfrica English (current) En Français Toggle navigation My Account Toggle navigation AllAfrica My Account English (current) En Français Ethiopia: From Military Victory to Political Settlement - Why Ethiopia's Real Test Lies Beyond Controlling Mekelle 19 October 2026 Addis Standard (Addis Ababa) Addis Abeba — Mekelle, the capital of Tigray Regional State, has now changed hands three times in six years. Federal forces took the city in November 2020, within a month of the last war beginning; Tigrayan forces retook it in June 2021 . On 3 October 2026, federal troops and the allied Tigray Peace Force entered it again , after the TPLF announced that it had withdrawn and that its regional administration would "temporarily move out" of the capital. The mood in parts of Addis Abeba is triumphant. It should be sober. This round began on 23 September, when Tigrayan forces launched an offensive into Afar and Amhara . The momentum soon reversed; government-aligned forces have since also entered Adigrat , near the Eritrean border, and Axum . On 11 October, according to local media, Getachew Reda, now the prime minister's adviser on East African affairs, declared the war over and said Tigray would be run by a federal command post for six months before elections. The TPLF leadership, now in the northern countryside, has announced a shift to "mobile warfare." Taking a city is a military event. Settling the question that produced the war is sociological: who belongs to the political community, on what terms, and who has the authority to decide. Follow us on WhatsApp | LinkedIn for the latest headlines My argument is this. The war is rooted in an unresolved bargain at home; the regional realignment that now sets rival Gulf- and Egypt-led alignments against each other across the Horn raises its stakes and supplies its patrons. Ethiopia is stronger in external terms than at any point since 2018, yet thinner in the social foundations of authority: the willing consent of its own regions. Whether Prime Minister Abiy Ahmed emerges as the Horn's pivotal statesman or as the manager of a permanent counterinsurgency depends on what Addis Abeba does with Mekelle, not on the fact of having taken it. Tigray's unfinished peace, Ethiopia's unsettled state The federal government's case deserves to be stated at full strength, because much of it is sound. The Pretoria Agreement of 2022 required the disarmament of Tigrayan forces, and disputes over disarmament and the TPLF's legal status were never resolved . In 2025 a TPLF faction forced Getachew Reda out of the interim administration ; in May 2026 the party reinstated the pre-war regional council, which elected Debretsion Gebremichael as president , outside the framework Pretoria had set. By mid-year, Tigray's authorities were declaring that the agreement "has collapsed," and on 23 September, it was Tigrayan forces that went on the offensive. No sovereign state tolerates a second army answering to a rival government. That case is strong, but it is not the whole account. A detailed Al Jazeera reconstruction found that while the TPLF retained an organizational and security role the agreement was meant to diminish , the federal government also failed to deliver important parts of the settlement. The June national elections were not held in Tigray at all . Meanwhile, Tigrayans lived what a contributor in these pages called peace on paper and suffering in practice . By May, Addis Standard was reporting allegations of forced conscription across Tigray , with opposition parties such as Salsay Weyane Tigray demanding an end to what Tigrayans call gifa. Prolonged deprivation converts political grievance into everyday humiliation, the raw material of mobilization. Tigrayan dissent also shows that Tigray is not a single political subject. Any settlement that treats the TPLF as the sole voice of Tigray, or all Tigrayans as the TPLF, will misread the society it seeks to pacify. Taking a city is a military event. Settling the question that produced the war is sociological." By September, Ethiopia contained two authorities claiming to govern the same territory, each with its own army. Charles Tilly called this condition multiple sovereignty and treated it as the defining feature of a revolutionary situation. The war is therefore less about resources or ideology than about statehood: whether Ethiopia's federation is a union of self-governing nations that may bargain with the center by force or a sovereign state that monopolizes legitimate coercion and negotiates only through its institutions. Alliance of the aggrieved Days before the offensive, seven armed movements, including the TPLF, the Amhara Fano National Movement, and the Oromo Liberation Army, announced an alliance pledging to work toward the fall of Abiy's government and its replacement by a charter-based transitional administration. Fano fought alongside federal forces against the TPLF in 2020-2022 , and Amhara and Tigrayan nationalists still claim the same land in Western Tigray. Sociologically, this is a negative coalition, bound by a shared adversary rather than a shared vision. Such coalitions are strong at the moment of mobilization and brittle at the moment of distribution, because what each member ultimately wants is indivisible: Welkait cannot belong to both Amhara and Tigray. The fissures also run through, not merely between, these constituencies. The Tigray Peace Force, a Tigrayan militia aligned with Addis Abeba , helped take Alamata and entered Mekelle beside federal troops, and Getachew Reda, once the TPLF's most visible spokesman, returned to the city as the face of federal authority. The war over Tigray is also, increasingly, a war within it. Yet a fractious coalition is not an impotent one. Fano holds towns in southern Wollo and northern Shewa , and the TPLF left Mekelle without a street battle, preserving its fighters, much as it withdrew to the highlands in 2020 before returning in 2021. Analysts at the Critical Threats Project judge the movement weaker than in the last war , citing thinner popular support and Ethiopia's improved drones. They may be right. But insurgencies need not win battles; they need only outlast a state's patience. After Mekelle: Control without consent The capture of Mekelle by federal forces has not ended multiple sovereignty; it has changed its form. Two governments in one region have become a government in the towns and an insurgency in the hills. The question now is whether the authority that holds Mekelle can become one Tigrayans obey without being compelled. The first days show how steep that climb will be. Federal forces did not inherit a city ready to be governed. Residents described a security vacuum and looting of government offices , and the UN reported that warehouses run by a UN agency and aid organizations had been looted . The fighting has been costly: hospital sources told the BBC that at least 52 civilians were killed in three days around Alamata , and a humanitarian source estimated at least 150,000 displaced in Afar . All this falls on a region already in drought, where, according to the regional disaster agency, 3.9 million people, more than half the population, needed emergency food assistance . An administration that arrives by arms will be judged by bread, and it will be judged quickly. A command post followed by elections has a logic, but it is an instrument of what sociologist Michael Mann called despotic power , the capacity to act without negotiating with society. Despotic power can take a city; only infrastructural power, the routine capacity to deliver law and services with local cooperation, can hold it. The Tigray Peace Force gives the federal presence a Tigrayan face, but it also risks turning a federal-regional war into an intra-Tigrayan one, in which those who fought beside Addis Abeba are seen by their neighbors as agents of conquest. Success over the next six months will be measured not in towns held but in whether cash, fuel, and food move; whether the displaced of Western Tigray can go home; and whether Tigrayans who belong to neither the TPLF nor the Tigray Peace Force can organize, compete, and win. Mandate and monopoly The Prosperity Party comfortably won June's elections , taking 438 of the 486 seats for which results were declared . The vote supplied a procedural mandate. It could not, by itself, supply what Max Weber treated as the substance of legitimacy: a belief among the governed that authority is rightful. Elections were not held in Tigray, Fano has held swathes of the Amhara countryside since 2023 , and the OLA has fought in Oromia since 2018. Before the vote, an Addis Standard op-ed described the ruling party's method as procedural authoritarianism , power exercised through rather than against formal institutions. Where institutions cannot carry competition, it migrates to arms. The National Dialogue Commission might have been a bridge, yet even its Tigray agenda-gathering forum had to be moved to Addis Abeba . Battlefield success can deepen state authority; Tilly's observation that war made the state is not wrong. But in Ethiopia, war has unmade regimes as often as it has made them; the Derg fell to a coalition of regional fronts. The temptation after Mekelle will be to treat armed opponents purely as criminals rather than as expressions of unresolved political questions. A Tigray election held under a command post, without credible guarantees for the TPLF's rivals or a path back for its rank and file, would reproduce the June pattern at regional scale: a mandate without consent. Abiy's two ledgers The external ledger is strong. In June, the IMF reported improving output, exports, reserves, and revenue, alongside declining inflation , as it reached agreement on the fifth review of Ethiopia's program. By external measures, Abiy is stronger than at any point in his tenure. The domestic ledger is harder. The coalition now arrayed against him includes his two most important wartime partners of 2020: Fano and Eritrea. Supporters of the government will say each broke away over its own ambitions: Fano over the reorganization of regional special forces , Asmara over a Pretoria process to which it was not a party . Critics see a pattern in which alliances rest on personal bargains rather than institutions and dissolve once those bargains are spent. Either way, Ethiopia's wartime friendships have proved less durable than its enmities. The 2019 Nobel laureate, honored for making peace with Eritrea, now accuses Asmara of sending troops into Tigray. In a February letter to Addis Standard, former foreign minister Gedu Andargachew said that Eritrean and Ethiopian forces operated "as a single force" until the Pretoria ceasefire , an account that contradicts the prime minister's own. An unreckoned war tends to seed the next one. If military advantage is now followed by political inclusion, Abiy will emerge as the Horn's indispensable statesman. If it is followed by reprisal and exclusion, he risks winning a war and losing the peace for a second time. Access to the sea and the logic of encirclement No issue has shaped the regional reading of this war more than Abiy's quest for the sea. He has called the loss of Assab a historical mistake whose reversal is "a matter of time," while insisting that Ethiopia has no intention to invade Eritrea . The war has turned that ambition into a concrete vulnerability. Fighting in Afar threatened the routes from Djibouti through which most Ethiopian imports, including fuel, pass . A state of Ethiopia's size that depends on a single corridor through a contested borderland is not simply a trading nation with a logistics problem; it is a sovereignty with a hostage. Since Mekelle fell, the Eritrean dimension has moved from allegation towards confrontation. Ethiopia has accused Eritrea of a territorial incursion and demanded the withdrawal of its troops and told the UN Security Council that Eritrean troops had advanced up to 60 kilometers into Tigray . Asmara denies any incursion and has asked the Council to intervene , calling Ethiopia's conduct a pretext to seize Assab. The scale of any Eritrean deployment has not been independently established. But on 5 October, in his re-inauguration address, Abiy reiterated that Ethiopia must have access to the Red Sea . Maritime access, national security, and the war have fused into one question. Addis Abeba's practical response has been quieter than its rhetoric and probably wiser. On 24 September, Abiy stood beside Djibouti's President Ismail Omar Guelleh to announce a $660 million refined-fuel pipeline from Damerjog to Dewele . The pipeline makes a neighbor a stakeholder in Ethiopia's security rather than an object of its ambition. This magazine warned in 2024 that a country ravaged by internal crises can neither shape nor safeguard its national interest . The most serious threat to Ethiopia's maritime lifeline in 2026 has come not from foreign navies but from fighting in Afar, Amhara, and Tigray. Sea access is a legitimate national aspiration, but its first line of defense runs through domestic peace. Two blocs, both fluid Those coastal anxieties have found patrons. The Institute for Economics and Peace describes an emerging UAE-Israel-Ethiopia axis set against a Saudi-Egypt-Türkiye reaction . In July, Saudi Arabia launched a 14-nation Red Sea maritime coalition that included Egypt, Türkiye, Sudan, Djibouti, and Somalia, but not the UAE. On 4 October, the day after Mekelle fell, the leaders of Egypt, Eritrea, Somalia, and Sudan converged at El Alamein; their declaration did not name Ethiopia but asserted that Red Sea governance belongs to littoral states and restated Egypt's demands on the dam . Sudan is where the blocs collide. Sudan's army-aligned government has alleged that drone attacks on its territory originated from Ethiopia , which Addis Abeba rejects as baseless , and a Reuters investigation reported that Ethiopia was hosting an RSF training camp . Ethiopia's army chief, in turn, accuses foreign powers of "pushing, supporting, and supplying" the new alliance , naming Eritrea, Sudan, and Egypt, all of which deny it. On 1 October, Ethiopia closed its embassy in Eritrea and expelled Eritrean diplomats ; Asmara severed relations . Whatever the truth of each allegation, proxy war is a currency that circulates in both directions. Ethiopia has won wars before. What it has rarely done is win the peace that follows." The Nile runs through the same ledger. The Grand Ethiopian Renaissance Dam was inaugurated in September 2025 , and in February Cairo denied a report that it had offered to help Ethiopia secure Red Sea access in exchange for flexibility on the dam. The two dossiers have become one bargaining space. No battle changes hydrology; what war changes is the cost of Egyptian pressure. If Ethiopia emerges cohesive, pressure exerted through its internal fault lines loses value. If the war drags on, Cairo gains leverage without firing a shot. These alignments are not alliances. Somalia joined the El Alamein summit yet kept cooperating with Addis Abeba, and its president met Abiy as recently as 28 September . Ethiopia's BRICS membership, shared with Egypt and the UAE , is insurance, not protection. Washington, which let its Eritrea sanctions lapse, citing US interests in the Red Sea while also imposing visa restrictions on "hardline members" of the TPLF , offers neutrality, not guarantees. Neither camp can impose an order on the Horn. The decisive variable is Ethiopia's internal cohesion: a united Ethiopia is a regional pole; a divided one is a regional battlefield. The first is coerced consolidation, and it is now the government's declared path: a command post, a coalition fragmenting along its fault lines, and separate settlements with its members. It can succeed only if it brings a credible process on the disputed territories, reconstruction, an election open to Tigrayans of every persuasion, and a national dialogue that includes those who fought. That requires a political generosity the government has not yet demonstrated. The second is protracted insurgency. The TPLF has given up the towns, not the war. Its leaders have promised further operations from the northern highlands, the terrain from which it returned in 2021. A mobile campaign alongside Fano and the OLA would mean a war of attrition that drains the economy and invites proxy intervention. The third is regionalization, and it is no longer hypothetical: severed diplomatic relations, rival letters to the Security Council, and reported Eritrean deployments on Ethiopian soil, layered onto Sudan's war. The EU has urged both governments to de-escalate , and the International Crisis Group has called for former AU envoy Olusegun Obasanjo to be brought back into mediation and for Saudi Arabia and the UAE to coordinate to keep a Red Sea front from opening. The fourth is a positive-sum Ethiopia. It reaches the sea not by redrawing borders but by rewriting interests: a guaranteed port and corridor arrangement in which Eritrea keeps sovereignty, Ethiopia holds equity and access, and neighbors share in its markets. The dam generated 52 percent of Ethiopia's electricity-export revenue in 2025/26 , according to the state utility; the planned Bishoftu airport is billed as Africa's largest ; and a population of some 135 million could make Ethiopia the Horn's energy, logistics, and manufacturing center. The current confrontation makes this harder, not impossible, provided Addis Abeba trades the language of restitution for that of interdependence. Without peace, a young population becomes a recruiting pool rather than a dividend. The darker variant of success is a garrison state with a port: a coastline without peace, power without legitimacy. Decisive Victory: Political, not military The strongest possibility is a civic turn. Both camps in this war are multi-ethnic coalitions, each discovering that no ethnic project can secure itself alone. Sea-access nationalism already addresses citizens as Ethiopians rather than as members of ethnic nations, but it cannot substitute for a negotiated federal bargain. Exhaustion, a generation born after 1991 and integrating national markets, could yield a different consensus: citizenship as the basis of political claims, cultural rights protected, Article 39 reinterpreted by agreement, electoral rules rewarding cross-regional parties, and disputed territories under shared administration. Imposed from above, civic nationalism becomes assimilation; it must be chosen, in Renan's phrase, as a daily plebiscite. The balance of power in the Horn will not finally be decided at Assab, at the dam, or in Mekelle. It will be decided by whether the Ethiopian state can turn the loyalty of its citizens from a battlefield into a resource. This is the paradox of Ethiopian power: the more Ethiopia acts as a regional power, the more its internal fault lines become assets for its rivals. Abiy has shown he can survive, outmaneuver, and project; the question is whether he can include. Ethiopia has won wars before. What it has rarely done is win the peace that follows. That, not the fall of any city, is the victory worth seeking. AS Editor's Note : Tesfatsion Dominiko has a PhD in Sociology and Social Anthropology from Stellenbosch University. He also works as a freel
ethiopia.summary: Ethiopia's recent military control of Mekelle, the capital of Tigray, marks a significant shift in the ongoing conflict, which has seen the city change hands multiple times since 2020. Federal forces, alongside the Tigray Peace Force, re-entered Mekelle on October 3, 2026, following the TPLF's withdrawal. While the mood in Addis Ababa is celebratory, the situation remains complex. The war's roots lie in unresolved political grievances, with multiple authorities claiming governance over Tigray. The federal government faces challenges in establishing legitimacy and authority, as many Tigrayans view the TPLF as their representative. The humanitarian crisis in the region is dire, with millions needing assistance. The future stability of Ethiopia hinges on whether the federal government can gain the consent of Tigrayans and address the underlying sociopolitical issues rather than merely exert military control.

ethiopia.title: Ethiopia Warns Somaliland Recognition Could Strengthen Al-Shabaab, Somaliland Officials Push Back
ethiopia.content: Somalia: Ethiopia Warns Somaliland Recognition Could Strengthen Al-Shabaab, Somaliland Officials Push Back - allAfrica.com AllAfrica English (current) En Français Toggle navigation My Account Toggle navigation AllAfrica My Account English (current) En Français Somalia: Ethiopia Warns Somaliland Recognition Could Strengthen Al-Shabaab, Somaliland Officials Push Back 19 October 2026 Addis Standard (Addis Ababa) Addis Abeba — Ethiopia has warned that recognizing Somaliland could undermine regional counterterrorism efforts and strengthen Al-Shabaab, while Somaliland officials have rejected the security concerns, arguing that recognition would instead enhance regional stability and advance Ethiopia's economic and strategic interests. Speaking to i24NEWS' Middle East Now , Ethiopia's ambassador to Israel, Tesfaye Yetaye Anteneh, said recognition could prompt Somalia to demand the withdrawal of Ethiopian troops deployed in the country as part of regional counterterrorism operations. "The moment, for example, Ethiopia recognizes Somaliland, the Somali government will request Ethiopia to withdraw its troops from Somalia," Anteneh said, warning that Al-Shabaab could exploit the resulting security vacuum to launch attacks in Somalia, Somaliland and potentially Ethiopia. The ambassador's remarks come amid renewed fighting in northern Ethiopia and escalating tensions between Addis Abeba and Asmara, raising concerns about a wider regional confrontation . Ethiopia has accused Eritrea of violating its sovereignty by deploying troops inside Ethiopian territory, allegations Eritrea has rejected while accusing the Ethiopian government of preparing an "unprovoked war of aggression." Follow us on WhatsApp | LinkedIn for the latest headlines Anteneh said Eritrean forces remained in five localities in the Irob area of northern Ethiopia and called on the international community to pressure Asmara to withdraw its troops. Eritrea has also denied supporting Tigrayan rebel forces. Somaliland rejects security concerns Saeed Ibrahim, editor of the Somaliland Chronicle, challenged Ethiopia's assessment, arguing that Somaliland's record of preventing Al-Shabaab from establishing a significant operational presence within its territory undermines the ambassador's concerns. "I just don't agree with him," Ibrahim said during the i24NEWS programme, adding that he expected Ethiopia and Somaliland to resume negotiations over maritime access because of their closely aligned economic and strategic interests. Somaliland's ambassador to Israel, Mohamed Hagi, similarly argued in an October 15 post on X that recognizing the territory would strengthen Ethiopia's security rather than expose it to additional threats. "I am convinced the opposite is true: Ethiopia stands to gain enormous strategic, economic, and security benefits by recognising Somaliland, with zero security threat," Hagi wrote. He described Somaliland as "a strategic asset, not a security liability," citing its record against Al-Shabaab and piracy. Hagi also argued that Somalia's growing relationships with Ethiopia's regional rivals posed a greater strategic concern for Addis Abeba than Somaliland's pursuit of international recognition. Ethiopia's pursuit of sea access Ethiopia has been landlocked since Eritrea's independence in 1993 and remains heavily dependent on neighbouring Djibouti for maritime trade. Anteneh described securing sea access as an economic and strategic necessity for a country with a population exceeding 130 million. In January 2024, Ethiopia and Somaliland signed a memorandum of understanding proposing access to the coastline and the possibility of diplomatic recognition. The agreement triggered strong opposition from Somalia, which considers Somaliland part of its sovereign territory. Ethiopia has yet to formally recognize Somaliland, despite Israel becoming the first United Nations member state to do so in December 2025. Somaliland officials maintain that recognition would provide Ethiopia with economic opportunities through the strategic Port of Berbera on the Gulf of Aden while strengthening cooperation on regional security. The dispute has gained renewed international attention following remarks by US President Donald Trump describing Somaliland as a "totally different country" from Somalia. Although the comments prompted celebrations in Somaliland's capital, Hargeisa, no formal change in US recognition policy has been announced. For Addis Abeba, the question remains how to balance its pursuit of maritime access with its security cooperation with Somalia and the diplomatic consequences of recognizing Somaliland. Somaliland officials, meanwhile, argue that formal recognition would advance shared economic and security interests across the Horn of Africa. Read the original article on Addis Standard . ethiopia.summary: Ethiopia has expressed concerns that recognizing Somaliland could bolster Al-Shabaab and jeopardize regional counterterrorism efforts. Ethiopian Ambassador to Israel, Tesfaye Yetaye Anteneh, warned that such recognition might lead Somalia to demand the withdrawal of Ethiopian troops, creating a security vacuum that Al-Shabaab could exploit. In contrast, Somaliland officials argue that recognition would enhance stability and benefit Ethiopia's economic interests, citing Somaliland's effective prevention of Al-Shabaab's operational presence. Somaliland's ambassador to Israel, Mohamed Hagi, emphasized that recognition would provide Ethiopia with strategic advantages, particularly through access to the Port of Berbera. The ongoing dispute highlights the complexities of Ethiopia's pursuit of maritime access while maintaining security cooperation with Somalia.

ethiopia.title: Oromo Intellectuals Back Ola-Fano Membership in New Armed Alliance, Call for Inclusive Transition in Ethiopia
ethiopia.content: Ethiopia: Oromo Intellectuals Back Ola-Fano Membership in New Armed Alliance, Call for Inclusive Transition in Ethiopia - allAfrica.com AllAfrica English (current) En Français Toggle navigation My Account Toggle navigation AllAfrica My Account English (current) En Français Ethiopia: Oromo Intellectuals Back Ola-Fano Membership in New Armed Alliance, Call for Inclusive Transition in Ethiopia 19 October 2026 Addis Standard (Addis Ababa) Addis Abeba — A group of Oromo intellectuals and public figures has backed the Oromo Liberation Army's (OLA) participation in a newly formed opposition coalition that includes the Amhara Fano movement, describing the alliance as a potential opening to address Ethiopia's deepening political crisis while calling for an inclusive transition that safeguards the rights and political aspirations of all communities. In a statement released Saturday October 17, and titled "Statement by Oromo Intellectuals on Ethiopia's Political Crisis and the Need for an Inclusive Transition," the signatories described the formation of the Ethiopian Peoples' Forces Coalition for Survival, also known as the Alliance for Survival, and the OLA's participation in it as "a significant first step toward finding a way out of a protracted crisis." The statement comes amid a widening debate among Oromo political constituencies over the OLA's decision to join forces with movements whose historical grievances, political objectives and national aspirations differ significantly from those of the Oromo. While some question whether the alignment can "safeguard Oromo interests", others frame the coalition as a "northern front" against a government led by an Oromo prime minister. Supporters, meanwhile, argue that Ethiopia's interlocking conflicts and political grievances require cooperation among opposition forces that have long operated separately. Keep up with the latest headlines on WhatsApp | LinkedIn The intellectuals' statement makes the case for the third position, arguing that historical antagonisms should not prevent political cooperation when the country faces a crisis that threatens its stability and the rights of its peoples. However, their endorsement is accompanied by a warning that removing the current government would not, by itself, guarantee democracy, peace or justice. "The weakening or removal of an existing political order does not automatically produce democracy, peace, or justice," the signatories said, urging the alliance and other political stakeholders to establish a credible, inclusive transitional process. A new alliance amid Ethiopia's fractured opposition landscape The Alliance for Survival was announced on September 20, 2026 , bringing together seven opposition and armed groups: the Amhara Fano National Movement (AFNM), the OLA, the Tigray People's Liberation Front (TPLF), the Ogaden National Liberation Front (ONLF), the Afar National United Revolutionary Front (ANURF), the Benishangul Peoples' Liberation Movement and the Gumuz Peoples' Democratic Movement. The coalition announced its intention to "remove" Prime Minister Abiy Ahmed's government militarily and establish a transitional administration, citing nationwide insecurity, armed conflict, displacement, poverty and human rights violations. For far too long, Ethiopia's opposition political landscape has been characterized by cycles of violence, mutual suspicion, and division Its formation brought together groups with distinct political objectives and constituencies, including former adversaries associated with the war in the Tigray region. Internationally, the alliance's formation drew criticism from several countries and blocs, including the European Union . Less widely reported, however, is the debate it has sparked among Oromos in Ethiopia and abroad, which made OLA's participation particularly contentious because of the historical and political divisions between Oromo and Amhara constituencies and the competing interpretations of what cooperation with Fano could mean for Oromo national aspirations. The intellectuals argue that Ethiopia's opposition landscape has been weakened by fragmentation, mutual suspicion and conflicts between communities that have diverted attention from underlying political grievances. "For far too long, Ethiopia's opposition political landscape has been characterized by cycles of violence, mutual suspicion, and division," they said. They further accused the government of repeatedly turning legitimate political grievances into "horizontal conflicts between communities," deepening mistrust and ethnic antagonisms while making collective political solutions more difficult. The statement's central argument is that Ethiopia's multiple conflicts cannot be resolved sustainably if political forces remain divided along historical, ethnic and ideological lines. OLA-Fano alignment divides Oromo opinion The OLA's participation has intensified debate among Oromo political constituencies, with disagreements centering on whether cooperation with Fano is a necessary strategic response to the national crisis or a potentially damaging compromise of Oromo political interests. One position rejects the alliance on the grounds that a shared opposition to the federal government does not resolve fundamental differences over national self-determination, historical accountability, territory and security. Supporters of this perspective argue that the OLA cooperation with Fano will not "subordinate Oromo aspirations" to a broader coalition's political objectives. A second position interprets the alliance as a "northern political and military front" against a government led by an Oromo prime minister. Supporters of this framing present the OLA's participation as contradictory to the movement's stated commitment to "Oromo rights and political aspirations." A third position defends the coalition as a pragmatic response to a nationwide crisis that individual opposition movements have been unable to resolve independently. Its proponents argue that cooperation need not mean "ideological convergence or the abandonment of distinct national aspirations"; rather, it can create an opportunity to pursue a common political opening while addressing disagreements through negotiation. The intellectuals' statement aligns with the third position, arguing that Oromo political aspirations and rights must remain central to any political process without being pursued in isolation from the legitimate aspirations of other peoples. "Whatever differences exist regarding the country's past and future, the peoples of Ethiopia must not be made enemies of one another while their common political grievances remain unresolved and their shared future uncertain," they said. "The struggle for justice and freedom must not become a struggle between communities," the statement added. The argument places responsibility on the alliance to demonstrate that its members can cooperate without sacrificing the rights, dignity and political agency of the communities they claim to represent. OLA leadership defends participation The debate has also drawn responses from the OLA leadership . OLA leader Kumsa Dirribaa, popularly known as Jaal Marroo, and his senior adviser, Jaal Jireenyaa Guddataa , have appeared in various media interviews to defend the decision of the group to participate in the coalition. Jaal Marroo admitted that there were around 20 meetings that took place between OLA and the remaining members of the Alliance prior to its announcement. Both have also argued that the OLA should not remain isolated from other opposition forces at a time when the Oromo people are facing what they describe as one of "the most brutal regimes" in their history. In the letter issued over the weekend, the group of intellectuals and public figures do not dismiss the concerns being raised in the ongoing debates. They call on Oromo civic actors, intellectuals and political stakeholders to scrutinize the alliance's objectives, commitments and long-term implications, while cautioning against rejecting it reflexively because of historical antagonisms or partisan interests. "Legitimate questions concerning emerging political alignments, their objectives, commitments, and long-term implications must be examined openly and critically," they said. The crisis now engulfing the entire country began in Oromia eight years ago The statement also urges the alliance and its constituent organizations to establish "credible mechanisms for resolving disagreements." Intellectuals link national crisis to grievances in Oromia The signatories argue that the crisis now affecting Ethiopia has deep roots in Oromia, where the conflict between government forces and the OLA has persisted for years. "The crisis now engulfing the entire country began in Oromia eight years ago," the statement said. The intellectuals also cited a statement they attributed to the head of the Oromia Prosperity Party: "We do not bother to catch the fish (the OLA); we will rather drain the sea (the Oromo)." They argue that the statement reflected a policy of collective punishment against the Oromo population, which they describe as the OLA's social base, and contend that the consequences included civilian deaths, displacement and widespread suffering. These are allegations and characterizations made by the signatories. Their broader argument is that militarized responses to political opposition have contributed to a nationwide crisis in which multiple communities face insecurity, displacement and political exclusion. "A political arrangement that protects the rights, dignity, and agency of all communities offers a more sustainable basis for addressing the country's interconnected crises," they said. Cooperation does not require forgetting history. It requires confronting history honestly and refusing to remain its prisoners For the signatories, the challenge is to ensure that cooperation across political divides does not come at the expense of Oromo aspirations or the rights of other communities. Call for a credible and inclusive transition The intellectuals' most consequential qualification concerns what would follow the removal of the current government. They warn that without a credible transitional arrangement, Ethiopia risks reproducing existing patterns of exclusion and political domination under a different configuration of power. The statement calls for a process involving "all relevant political stakeholders, including armed and unarmed opposition groups, civil society, and representatives of Ethiopia's diverse nations and nationalities." Such a transition, the signatories argue, must respect distinct political identities and legitimate national aspirations, protect civilians and allow Ethiopia's peoples to determine their political future freely, without coercion or predetermined outcomes. The signatories called on the Alliance to move beyond military coordination and develop a credible political framework capable of accommodating its members' divergent objectives. The statement, signed by prominent figures including Professor Mohammed Hassan, Professor Ezekiel Gabbisa, Baqqalaa Garbaa, Dr. Milkeessaa Miidhagaa, Dr. Bayaan Asoobaa and Jaal Jireenyaa Guddataa, presents cooperation as an opportunity to break from the fragmentation that has characterized Ethiopia's opposition politics . "Cooperation does not require forgetting history," the signatories said. "It requires confronting history honestly and refusing to remain its prisoners." Read the original article on Addis Standard . ethiopia.summary: A group of Oromo intellectuals has expressed support for the Oromo Liberation Army's (OLA) involvement in a new opposition coalition, the Ethiopian Peoples' Forces Coalition for Survival, which includes the Amhara Fano movement. They view this alliance as a potential solution to Ethiopia's escalating political crisis and advocate for an inclusive transition that respects the rights of all communities. The statement highlights the necessity of cooperation among historically divided groups to address underlying political grievances. However, it also warns that merely removing the current government will not ensure democracy or justice. The intellectuals call for a credible transitional process involving diverse political stakeholders to prevent further exclusion and conflict. The OLA's participation has sparked debate among Oromo constituencies, with differing opinions on whether it serves or undermines Oromo interests. The statement emphasizes the importance of addressing historical grievances while pursuing a unified political future.

ethiopia.title: Nile and Red Sea Inseparable Pillars Capable of Creating Regional Cooperation, Integration: Researchers - ENA English
ethiopia.summary: Researchers have emphasized the interconnectedness of the Nile and Red Sea as vital components for fostering regional cooperation and integration in East Africa. They argue that these two bodies of water are not only crucial for the ecological and economic stability of the region but also serve as platforms for collaborative initiatives among neighboring countries. By leveraging the resources and strategic significance of the Nile and Red Sea, nations can enhance trade, address environmental challenges, and promote sustainable development. The researchers advocate for a unified approach to managing these waterways, highlighting the potential benefits of regional partnerships in achieving long-term stability and prosperity.

ethiopia.title: Sodo Woreda Attacks Leave 11 Dead as Residents Plead for Federal Intervention - Borkena
ethiopia.summary: In Sodo Woreda, a series of violent attacks have resulted in the deaths of 11 individuals, prompting local residents to urgently call for federal intervention. The violence has raised concerns about security and stability in the region, with community members expressing fear for their safety. Eyewitnesses report that the attacks were carried out by armed groups, leading to widespread panic among the population. Residents are appealing to the federal government to take immediate action to restore order and protect them from further violence. The situation remains tense as the community grapples with the aftermath of the attacks and seeks assistance to prevent future incidents.

ethiopia.title: Can diplomacy prevent an Ethiopia-Eritrea war as Tigray gets a new administration? - DW.com
ethiopia.summary: As Ethiopia establishes a new administration in the Tigray region, concerns are rising about potential conflict with Eritrea. The recent political changes in Tigray could exacerbate tensions between the two nations, particularly given their historical animosities and the ongoing humanitarian crisis in the region. Diplomatic efforts are being called upon to mitigate the risk of war, with international stakeholders urging dialogue and cooperation. Analysts emphasize the importance of addressing underlying issues to foster stability and peace. The situation remains precarious, and the effectiveness of diplomatic interventions will be crucial in preventing escalation into armed conflict.

ethiopia.title: Ethiopia’s Naval Experience Contributes to Red Sea Security: Aregawi Berhe - ENA English
ethiopia.summary: Ethiopia's naval experience is playing a significant role in enhancing security in the Red Sea, according to Aregawi Berhe, the Director-General of the Ethiopian Maritime Affairs Authority. He emphasized that Ethiopia's strategic position and its commitment to maritime security are crucial for regional stability. The country has been actively involved in collaborative efforts with neighboring nations to address security challenges in the Red Sea, including piracy and illegal fishing. Aregawi highlighted the importance of building a capable navy and fostering partnerships to ensure safe navigation and protect maritime resources. Ethiopia's engagement in maritime security reflects its broader goals of contributing to peace and stability in the region.

ethiopia.title: Ethiopia's national security imperative: Alliance with Israel and Somaliland - The Jerusalem Post
ethiopia.summary: Ethiopia is strengthening its national security by forging alliances with Israel and Somaliland. This strategic partnership aims to enhance military cooperation and intelligence sharing, addressing regional threats and instability. The collaboration with Israel is particularly significant, as it provides Ethiopia with advanced technology and expertise in counter-terrorism efforts. Meanwhile, the alliance with Somaliland is focused on bolstering security in the Horn of Africa, where Ethiopia faces challenges from various militant groups. These alliances are seen as essential for Ethiopia to safeguard its interests and maintain stability in a volatile region. The Ethiopian government emphasizes that these partnerships will contribute to a more secure and prosperous future for the nation.

ethiopia.title: Crisis in Central Ethiopia: 11 Dead as Armed Raids Devastate East Gurage - EthiopiaToday
ethiopia.summary: In East Gurage, Central Ethiopia, armed raids have resulted in the deaths of 11 individuals, exacerbating an ongoing crisis in the region. The violence has led to widespread fear and displacement among local communities. Authorities are struggling to maintain order as tensions rise, with reports of increased attacks and retaliatory violence. The situation has drawn attention from humanitarian organizations, which are concerned about the safety and well-being of affected populations. Efforts to restore peace and provide assistance are underway, but challenges remain significant as the conflict continues to escalate. The government has been urged to take decisive action to address the root causes of the violence and protect civilians.

ethiopia.title: News: Ethiopia warns Somaliland recognition could strengthen Al-Shabaab, Somaliland officials push back - Addis Standard
ethiopia.summary: Ethiopia has issued a warning that recognizing Somaliland as an independent state could bolster the influence of Al-Shabaab, the militant group operating in the region. Ethiopian officials argue that such recognition might destabilize the Horn of Africa and exacerbate security challenges. In response, Somaliland officials have pushed back against this assertion, emphasizing their desire for international recognition and asserting that their independence would not contribute to the strengthening of Al-Shabaab. They argue that Somaliland has maintained relative peace and stability compared to the rest of Somalia. The ongoing debate highlights the complex geopolitical dynamics in the region, as various stakeholders weigh the implications of Somaliland's quest for recognition against the backdrop of security concerns.

somalia.title: Somalia, FAO and Norway Meet to Strengthen El Niño Preparedness as Flood Risks Mount - FTL Somalia
somalia.summary: Somalia, in collaboration with the Food and Agriculture Organization (FAO) and Norway, is taking proactive measures to enhance preparedness for potential El Niño-related flooding. As the risk of floods increases due to changing weather patterns, the meeting focused on strategies to mitigate the impact on vulnerable communities. The discussions emphasized the importance of early warning systems, improved agricultural practices, and community resilience initiatives. The FAO highlighted the need for coordinated efforts to ensure food security and protect livelihoods in the face of climate challenges. Norway's involvement underscores the international commitment to support Somalia in addressing these pressing environmental issues. The partnership aims to strengthen local capacities and enhance response mechanisms to safeguard affected populations.

somalia.title: Somali Army Chief Meets U.S. Chargé d’Affaires to Strengthen Defence Cooperation - FTL Somalia
somalia.summary: Somali Army Chief General Odowa Yusuf Rageh met with the U.S. Chargé d’Affaires, Larry André, to discuss enhancing defense cooperation between Somalia and the United States. The meeting focused on strategies to combat terrorism and improve the capabilities of the Somali National Army. General Rageh emphasized the importance of U.S. support in strengthening Somalia's security forces, particularly in the fight against the militant group Al-Shabaab. The discussions also highlighted ongoing efforts to stabilize the region and ensure peace and security in Somalia. Both officials expressed commitment to deepening the partnership and addressing security challenges collaboratively.

somalia.title: Somalia’s Aid Paradox: Saving lives, sustaining dependency - Addis Standard
somalia.summary: The article discusses the complex situation in Somalia regarding international aid, highlighting a paradox where humanitarian assistance saves lives but may also perpetuate dependency. While aid is crucial for addressing immediate needs, such as food insecurity and health crises, it can create a cycle of reliance that undermines local development and self-sufficiency. Critics argue that without a shift towards sustainable solutions, including investment in local economies and infrastructure, the country may remain trapped in a cycle of aid dependency. The article emphasizes the need for a balanced approach that combines immediate relief efforts with long-term strategies to empower communities and foster resilience.

somalia.title: Somalia’s Ruling Party Confirms Senator Garyare as Candidate for Galmudug Deputy Leader - Dawan Africa
somalia.summary: Somalia's ruling party has officially confirmed Senator Abdiqadir Mohamed Nur Garyare as its candidate for the position of Deputy Leader of Galmudug. The announcement comes as part of the party's strategy to strengthen its influence in the region. Senator Garyare, who has previously held various political roles, is expected to play a significant role in the governance of Galmudug if elected. The party's decision reflects its commitment to promoting experienced leaders in key positions to enhance stability and development in the area. The election for the Deputy Leader is anticipated to take place soon, with Garyare's candidacy likely to attract considerable attention and support from party members and constituents alike.

somalia.title: Somalia aviation authority, IATA sign agreement to strengthen safety oversight - Hiiraan Online
somalia.summary: The Somalia Civil Aviation Authority (SCAA) has signed a significant agreement with the International Air Transport Association (IATA) aimed at enhancing safety oversight in the country's aviation sector. This partnership is expected to improve regulatory frameworks and operational standards, ultimately fostering a safer flying environment in Somalia. The agreement includes provisions for training and capacity-building initiatives for local aviation personnel, ensuring compliance with international safety standards. The collaboration reflects Somalia's commitment to developing its aviation industry and enhancing air travel safety, which is crucial for economic growth and connectivity in the region.

somalia.title: The human cost of surging US air strikes in Somalia - Al Jazeera
somalia.summary: The article discusses the increasing number of U.S. air strikes in Somalia and their significant human cost. While these strikes are aimed at combating the militant group al-Shabaab, they have resulted in numerous civilian casualties and displacement. Local communities report that the strikes often miss their intended targets, leading to tragic consequences for innocent bystanders. Human rights organizations have raised concerns about the lack of accountability and transparency surrounding these military operations. The article highlights the complex dynamics of the conflict in Somalia, where the U.S. military's actions are intended to support the Somali government but often exacerbate the humanitarian crisis. As the air strikes continue to rise, the impact on civilians remains a critical issue that demands attention and action from both the U.S. government and international community.

somalia.title: Somalia seeks livestock exports to Iraq as countries move to revive joint committee - Hiiraan Online
somalia.summary: Somalia is aiming to enhance its livestock exports to Iraq as both nations work towards revitalizing a joint committee focused on trade and economic cooperation. The initiative comes amid efforts to strengthen bilateral relations and boost Somalia's economy through increased trade opportunities. The joint committee, which has been inactive, is expected to facilitate discussions on various sectors, including agriculture and livestock, to foster mutual benefits. Somalia's livestock sector is a vital part of its economy, and expanding exports to Iraq could provide significant financial support. The revival of this committee reflects a broader strategy by Somalia to engage with international markets and improve its trade dynamics.

somalia.title: Families fleeing Somalia crises find bleak prospects in Dadaab refugee camps - Hiiraan Online
somalia.summary: Families fleeing crises in Somalia are facing dire conditions in the Dadaab refugee camps in Kenya. The camps, originally established to accommodate a temporary influx of refugees, are now home to over 200,000 people, leading to overcrowding and limited resources. Many refugees are struggling with inadequate access to food, clean water, and healthcare. The ongoing conflict, drought, and famine in Somalia have driven families to seek safety, but the camps offer little hope for a better future. Aid organizations are overwhelmed and unable to meet the growing needs of the population, leaving many refugees in a state of uncertainty and despair. The situation highlights the urgent need for international support and sustainable solutions to address the challenges faced by displaced families.

somalia.title: Libya and Somalia Discuss Economic and Trade Cooperation - Libya Herald
somalia.summary: Libya and Somalia have engaged in discussions to enhance economic and trade cooperation between the two nations. The talks focused on potential partnerships in various sectors, aiming to boost bilateral trade and investment. Both countries expressed a commitment to strengthening their economic ties and exploring opportunities for collaboration. The discussions are part of broader efforts to foster regional cooperation and development. Officials from both sides highlighted the importance of sharing resources and expertise to achieve mutual benefits. The meetings reflect a growing interest in establishing stronger economic relationships within the region.

somalia.title: Somalia beat Rwanda on penalties to reach CECAFA U-17 final - Hiiraan Online
somalia.summary: Somalia triumphed over Rwanda in a tense penalty shootout to secure a place in the CECAFA U-17 final. The match ended in a draw after regulation and extra time, leading to penalties where Somalia emerged victorious. This win marks a significant achievement for the Somali U-17 team, showcasing their resilience and skill in a competitive tournament. The final will see Somalia compete for the championship title, further highlighting the progress of youth football in the region.

football.title: الهلال السوداني يصنع الحدث و"غربال" على موعد مع المجد - شبكة تواصل الإخبارية
football.summary: الهلال السوداني حقق إنجازًا كبيرًا في مسيرته الكروية، حيث تمكن من الوصول إلى مراحل متقدمة في المنافسات القارية. اللاعب "غربال" كان له دور بارز في هذا النجاح، حيث أظهر مهاراته العالية وأداءه المتميز في المباريات. الجماهير تتطلع إلى المزيد من الإنجازات، مع آمال كبيرة في تحقيق الألقاب. الهلال يسعى لتعزيز مكانته في الساحة الرياضية، ويبدو أن الفريق في طريقه لتحقيق المجد الذي يطمح إليه.

football.title: الهلال السوداني والسويحلي الليبي يقتربان من مجموعات دوري الأبطال - مانكيش نت
football.summary: اقترب فريق الهلال السوداني وفريق السويحلي الليبي من التأهل إلى مرحلة المجموعات في دوري أبطال أفريقيا. جاء ذلك بعد الأداء القوي الذي قدمه الفريقان في المباريات التمهيدية. الهلال السوداني حقق نتائج إيجابية في مبارياته السابقة، مما يعزز فرصه في التأهل، بينما تمكن السويحلي من تقديم عرض قوي في التصفيات. يتطلع كلا الفريقين إلى تحقيق النجاح في المرحلة المقبلة من البطولة، حيث تعتبر هذه المنافسة فرصة كبيرة لإظهار مهاراتهم على المستوى القاري.

football.title: الهلال السوداني والسويحلي الليبي يقتربان من دور المجموعات في دوري ابطال افريقيا - Elsport
football.summary: اقترب فريق الهلال السوداني وفريق السويحلي الليبي من التأهل إلى دور المجموعات في دوري أبطال أفريقيا بعد أدائهما القوي في التصفيات. حيث حقق الهلال السوداني فوزاً مهماً على منافسه في مباراة الذهاب، مما يعزز فرصه في التأهل. من جهة أخرى، قدم السويحلي الليبي عرضاً مميزاً في مباراته، مما يضعه في موقف جيد للتقدم في البطولة. يتطلع كلا الفريقين إلى تحقيق نتائج إيجابية في مباريات الإياب لضمان مكانهما في دور المجموعات، حيث تعتبر هذه المرحلة من البطولة ذات أهمية كبيرة للأندية الأفريقية.

football.title: الهلال السوداني يحسم مواجهة سيداما بونا ويقترب من التأهل الأفريقي - اخبار السودان
football.summary: حقق فريق الهلال السوداني فوزًا مهمًا على سيداما بونا الإثيوبي في مباراة ضمن تصفيات دوري أبطال أفريقيا، مما يقربه من التأهل للمرحلة التالية. انتهت المباراة بفوز الهلال بنتيجة 2-0، حيث سجل الأهداف كل من اللاعب محمد عبد الرحمن واللاعب وليد الشعلة. قدم الفريق أداءً قويًا خلال المباراة، مما ساهم في تعزيز فرصه في المنافسة على اللقب الأفريقي. بهذا الفوز، يواصل الهلال مسيرته الناجحة في البطولة ويعزز من موقفه في المجموعة.

football.title: موعد بث مواجهة الهلال وسيداما والقنوات الناقلة للقاء المرتقب اليوم - موقع رادار
football.summary: تقام اليوم مواجهة مرتقبة بين فريق الهلال وسيداما، حيث ينتظر عشاق كرة القدم هذه المباراة بفارغ الصبر. ستبدأ المباراة في تمام الساعة 8:00 مساءً بتوقيت مكة المكرمة. سيتم بث اللقاء عبر عدة قنوات، منها القناة الرياضية السعودية، بالإضافة إلى منصات البث المباشر على الإنترنت. يُعتبر هذا اللقاء مهمًا للفريقين، حيث يسعى الهلال لتحقيق الفوز لتعزيز موقفه في البطولة، بينما يأمل سيداما في تقديم أداء قوي أمام خصمهم.

football.title: موعد بث مواجهة الهلال وسيداما والقنوات الناقلة للقاء المرتقب اليوم - موقع رادار
football.summary: تستعد جماهير كرة القدم لمتابعة مواجهة الهلال وسيداما اليوم، حيث من المقرر أن تنطلق المباراة في تمام الساعة 8:00 مساءً بتوقيت مكة المكرمة. ستقام المباراة في إطار المنافسات القارية، مما يزيد من حماس المشجعين. يمكن متابعة اللقاء عبر عدة قنوات ناقلة، منها قناة "SSC" التي تمتلك حقوق البث، بالإضافة إلى منصات البث المباشر. يُتوقع أن تكون المباراة مثيرة، حيث يسعى الهلال لتحقيق الفوز وتعزيز موقفه في البطولة.

football.title: السويحلي يسقط الترجي وتعادل صنداونز.. نتائج ذهاب دور الـ32 من دوري أبطال أفريقيا - يلاكورة
football.summary: حقق فريق السويحلي فوزًا مهمًا على الترجي التونسي في ذهاب دور الـ32 من دوري أبطال أفريقيا، مما يعزز آماله في التأهل للدور المقبل. في مباراة أخرى، انتهت مواجهة صنداونز الجنوب أفريقي مع منافسه بالتعادل، مما يجعل الأمور مفتوحة في مباراة الإياب. تأتي هذه النتائج في إطار المنافسات القوية التي يشهدها دوري أبطال أفريقيا، حيث يسعى كل فريق لتحقيق أفضل أداء لضمان التأهل.

football.title: مدرب الهلال يتوعد سيداما ويثق في بلوغ مجموعات دوري الأبطال - winwin
football.summary: مدرب الهلال، رامون دياز، أعرب عن ثقته في قدرة فريقه على تجاوز عقبة سيداما الإثيوبي في التصفيات المؤهلة لدوري أبطال آسيا. خلال مؤتمر صحفي، أكد دياز أن الهلال يمتلك الإمكانيات اللازمة لتحقيق الفوز والتأهل إلى مرحلة المجموعات. وأشار إلى أهمية المباراة وضرورة التركيز على الأداء الجيد، مشددًا على أن الفريق جاهز تمامًا لمواجهة التحديات. كما أعرب عن تفاؤله بقدرة اللاعبين على تقديم مستوى مميز يضمن لهم النجاح في هذه المرحلة الحاسمة.

football.title: الهلال السوداني يقترب من مجموعات الأبطال بثنائية.. ومولودية الجزائر في ورطة - الجمهور الإخباري
football.summary: حقق فريق الهلال السوداني فوزاً مهماً على ضيفه مولودية الجزائر بنتيجة 2-0 في مباراة الذهاب من الدور التمهيدي لدوري أبطال أفريقيا. بهذا الانتصار، اقترب الهلال من التأهل إلى مرحلة المجموعات، حيث قدم أداءً قوياً واستطاع تسجيل هدفين في الشوط الثاني. في المقابل، يواجه مولودية الجزائر تحديات كبيرة بعد هذه الخسارة، مما يزيد من ضغوط الفريق قبل مباراة الإياب. يحتاج الفريق الجزائري إلى تحقيق نتيجة إيجابية في المباراة القادمة لضمان فرصه في التأهل.

football.title: الهلال السوداني يضرب في إثيوبيا ويقترب من مجموعات أبطال أفريقيا - السودان اليوم
football.summary: حقق فريق الهلال السوداني فوزاً مهماً على مضيفه فاسيل كيتيما الإثيوبي في مباراة الذهاب من الدور التمهيدي لدوري أبطال أفريقيا. انتهت المباراة بفوز الهلال بنتيجة 2-0، مما يعزز فرصه في التأهل إلى مرحلة المجموعات. سجل أهداف الهلال كل من اللاعب محمد عبد الرحمن واللاعب وليد الشعلة، حيث قدم الفريق أداءً مميزاً خلال اللقاء. ومن المقرر أن تقام مباراة الإياب في السودان، حيث يسعى الهلال إلى تأكيد تفوقه وضمان التأهل. يعتبر هذا الفوز خطوة إيجابية نحو تحقيق طموحات الفريق في البطولة الأفريقية.
